title: How to make a 3D floor plan from a sketch and photos
heading: How to make a furnished 3D floor plan from a sketch and room photos
description: Turn a hand-drawn floor plan and photos of your rooms into a furnished 3D flat with AI and try new furniture ideas. No CAD skills needed. Step by step in SOMA.
summary: A floor plan sketch and photos of each room become a furnished 3D model of a flat, built by an AI agent in SOMA, with a round dining table tried out on the side.

video.title: From Floor Plan to Furnished 3D Flat with AI (No CAD Skills Needed) | SOMA

chapters.label: A round table in the kitchen

answer: Draw your floor plan with the main measurements, take a few photos of each room, and import both into SOMA. Then ask the AI agent to build the walls, doors and windows from the sketch, and to add the furniture it sees in the photos in the right rooms. The furniture is made of simple shapes and the agent tells you which sizes it had to guess, so the result is good for planning and trying ideas, not a replacement for an exact survey.
need: SOMA, free for Windows, macOS and Linux.

A ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, or an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenCode, to sign in to SOMA AI. SOMA is free, the AI runs on your plan or key. The cheapest way to start is an OpenCode Go subscription for about $10 a month.
A sketch of your floor plan as a photo or image: the rooms, doors and windows, and a few measurements taken with a tape measure.
A few photos of each room, named so you can tell them apart (for example kitchen-1.jpg, living-1.jpg).
In the video the agent is Claude Code; SOMA AI, built into SOMA, works the same way.

steps.title: Bring in your sketch and photos
text: Click New model on the start page. Open the SOMA AI tab in the agent area on the right; the first time, sign in with your ChatGPT plan or paste an API key.
Click Import and pick the floor plan sketch and the room photos. SOMA copies them into the folder inputs of the model, where the agent can find them. Click a file in Files to look at it.
The sketch can be simple: the rooms, the doors and windows, and a few measurements, just as you would draw your own flat with a tape measure.

image.alt: The hand-drawn floor plan opened in SOMA, with bedroom, hall, bath, living room and kitchen with dining area and their measurements, and the imported photos listed in Files

steps.title: Let the agent build the walls
text: First the empty flat. Tell the agent which file to read and what to build. Use the name of your own sketch file.
The agent reads the sketch, builds the model and checks the result. This takes a few minutes. You get every wall, door opening and window where the sketch has them.
steps.prompt: Build my flat in 3D from the sketch inputs/floor-plan.png: floor, walls, door openings and windows, as drawn. No ceiling.

image.alt: The empty flat in 3D: floor, outer and inner walls with door openings and windows, without a ceiling

steps.title: Furnish it from the photos
text: Now ask the agent to look at the photos and add the furniture it sees. It goes through them room by room and builds every piece from simple boxes and cylinders.
When it is done, it tells you what it had to guess, like the size of the sofa, so you know what to check. Every piece is its own part, sorted by room in the structure tree.

To see it like a floor plan, click Top on the view cube and use Section along Z to cut the walls. In the video the agent picked up the red sofa and the sewing table, the old stove and the kitchen cabinet, the two beds with the wardrobe, and the bathtub.
steps.prompt: Now furnish it. The photos in inputs/ show each room. Add simple models of the furniture you see, in the right rooms.

image.alt: The furnished flat from above with the walls cut by a section: beds, wardrobe, bathtub, red sofa, tables, chairs and kitchen furniture in their rooms

steps.title: Try an idea: a round table
text: Click the piece you want to change in the 3D view, here the kitchen table. Click Send to agent in the card that appears, and say what you want.
The agent replaces the table and moves the chairs around it. Only the table and the chairs change, the rest of the flat stays as it is.
steps.prompt: Make this a round table, 1 m across, with four chairs around it. Make the diameter adjustable.

image.alt: Top view of the flat with the kitchen table clicked and highlighted in orange, and its card with the Send to agent button

steps.title: Change the size with a slider
text: Because you asked for an adjustable size, the table diameter shows up in Parameters in the sidebar. Drag the slider and SOMA rebuilds the flat by itself, no agent needed. For a whole flat each rebuild takes a few seconds.
Every change is saved as a version on the History timeline at the bottom, so you can try as many ideas as you like and always go back.

image.alt: The kitchen with a round table and four chairs, and the kitchen table diameter slider in the Parameters panel set to 1300 mm

tips: Build the empty flat first and furnish it in a second message. Smaller steps are easier to check and to correct.
Measure the main walls with a tape measure and write the numbers on the sketch. The more measurements, the closer the model.
Name the photos by room, for example kitchen-1.jpg, so the agent knows where each piece belongs.
Read what the agent says it had to guess, and correct the sizes that matter to you, for example: Make the sofa 2.2 m long.
When you ask for a change, say what should be adjustable. Then you can try sizes with a slider instead of asking again.
In the video the agent is Claude Code; SOMA AI, built into SOMA, works the same way.

faq.q: Can AI turn a floor plan sketch into a 3D model?
faq.a: Yes. An AI agent can read a photo or image of a hand-drawn floor plan and build the floor, walls, door openings and windows in 3D. It follows the measurements written on the sketch, so the result is as accurate as your sketch.

faq.q: Can AI furnish a room from photos?
faq.a: Yes, roughly. The agent looks at photos of each room and adds simple models of the furniture it sees, such as a sofa, beds, a wardrobe or a table, in the right rooms. The pieces are made of simple shapes, and the agent says which sizes it had to guess.

faq.q: Do I need CAD or 3D skills to make a 3D floor plan this way?
faq.a: No. You import your sketch and photos and say in plain words what you want. To change something, you click it and describe the change, or drag a slider in the Parameters panel.

faq.q: Is the 3D floor plan accurate enough for building work?
faq.a: No, treat it as a planning aid. It is only as exact as the measurements on your sketch, and the furniture is approximate. For renovation or building work, rely on a proper survey and plans from a professional.

faq.q: Is it free to make a 3D floor plan with SOMA?
faq.a: SOMA itself is free and open source. The AI agent runs on your own ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan or on an API key from a provider such as Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, which you pay for there.
